culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: In villages, cover shoulders and legs (long skirts or a sulu wrap for women, T-shirts and knee-length shorts for men). Remove hat and sunglasses and carry bags in your hands, not on the shoulder. Speak softly. Take shoes off at the door of any village building.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Present a sevusevu (a bundle of kava) to the chief to ask permission to enter village land, and follow seating etiquette at the ceremony. Ask before taking photos or entering homes or communal areas. Many villages consider touching someone's head disrespectful; ask about each village's tabu.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Tourism Fiji; village chiefs (customs vary by village).
culture-and-protocol.note: National village etiquette from Tourism Fiji, applying across the division; each village has its own tabu.

layers.authority: National Trust of Fiji (Sigatoka Sand Dunes National Park)
layers.process: Entry fees at Sigatoka Sand Dunes: adults F$10, international students with ID F$7, local students aged 6 to 17 F$5, children 5 and under free (no RBA or central bank rate held for FJD, so no A$ figure). Open daily 8am to 4:30pm, closed 1pm to 2pm, and on public holidays. Visits outside those hours can be arranged for extra fees. Rangers give help or guided tours on request; the page does not require a guide.
